name: Montane / cloud forest
notes: Persistently fog-soaked montane forest of low, gnarled, moss-laden trees with bamboo thickets, tree ferns and a heavy epiphyte load of bromeliads, orchids and liverworts; drawn on the Andes, Central America and the Afromontane belt.

emergent.name: Andean wax palm

growth.juvenile_note: The first seedling leaves are narrow undivided or two-lobed blades; for decades the young palm is a stemless rosette of stiff pinnate leaves, silvery-white beneath, on the shaded cloud-forest floor while the trunk base thickens underground. Only after roughly half a century does the smooth, wax-coated whitish trunk start to rise.
growth.source: Wikipedia Ceroxylon quindiuense (45 m, rarely 60 m; fruit 1.6-2 cm orange-red; minimum reproductive age ~80 yr); Sanin & Galeano 2011 Phytotaxa (Ceroxylon revision); long stemless phase and growth rate estimated from Andean wax-palm demography studies

emergent.source: Palm of Colombian and Peruvian Andes cloud forest; height 40-60 m. Tallest palm on Earth; waxy white trunk above the cloud forest. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

canopy.name: Big-leaf rhododendron

Leaves get smaller as the plant ages and starts to flower; seedlings start tiny on moss and need shelter, humidity and part shade.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhododendron sinogrande (tree to 12 m; leaves up to 70 cm, occasionally 90 x 35 cm; flowers up to 8 cm, late spring; 2,100-3,600 m); larger leaves on young plants, slow flowering (15+ yr from seed) and growth rates from horticultural experience (estimated)

canopy.name: Campbell's magnolia

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two thick oval cotyledons, then alternate, large soft oblong leaves. The sapling is a vigorous single-leadered, rather narrow upright tree (shoots up to ~1.2 m a year) with stout grey twigs; the big furry flower buds are absent for the first 15-30 years, and the crown only broadens into a spreading dome with age.
growth.source: PFAF (at least 20 yr from seed to flower; beetle pollinated; seed needs winter cold, may take 18 months); T. Stone 'Plant of the week' (15 yr white forms to 30 yr pink forms from seed, ~10 yr grafted; young trees add up to 4 ft/yr); Wikipedia (30 m, rarely 45; flowers 15-25 cm); lifespan estimated

Single-stemmed: wild plants do not sucker. Flowers once (after ~4-8 yr, later in cold highlands), then dies.
growth.source: Kew POWO (6-12 m, flowers after ~4-8 yr); Useful Tropical Plants (2-10 yr from germination to flowering, ~6 months flower to fruit, germination within ~3 months); Plant Biology 2022 enset reproductive/germination ecology study (T50 ~35-36 days); Tropical Conservation Science 2019 camera-trap study of enset flower and fruit visitors

growth.juvenile_note: Spores or broken shoot tips sprout into a green protonemal film on moist logs, soil or rock, from which creeping shoots arise. Each shoot becomes a flat, twice- to thrice-pinnate, fern-like frond 3-10 cm long, yellow-green to dark green, interwoven into a soft, lacy carpet; red setae with curved brown capsules rise from it in autumn and winter.
growth.source: Wikipedia Thuidium delicatulum (delicate fern moss of North and South America, Alaska to Brazil); moss floras (regularly 2-3-pinnate fronds on moist forest soil, logs and rock, capsules ripening autumn-winter). Spore-to-shoot time, spread rate (a few cm a year) and patch age estimated from pleurocarpous forest mosses.

growth.juvenile_note: Soredia or broken bits lodge on twigs and bark and grow into a tiny pale grey-green tuft a few mm tall, fixed by a blackened basal holdfast. Young thalli are shrubby and upright with short side fibrils; as they lengthen they bend over and hang as a beard of stringy, branched strands, each with a stretchy white central cord that shows when a strand is gently pulled apart.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Usnea): thalli from a few mm in polluted air to over 3 m, spread by fragments, soredia or isidia and by spores, very sensitive to sulphur dioxide, slow-growing in nature. Growth (on the order of 1 cm a year), establishment and ages estimated from pendulous beard lichens.

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-like seed germinates (with a mycorrhizal fungus) into a tiny green protocorm; first leaf and roots follow after 2-3 months. Seedlings are miniature reed-stems: thin upright canes with two rows of small fleshy leaves, forming a small tuft. Old flower spikes often grow keikis (plantlets with aerial roots) that drop and root, so clumps spread; each cane lives a few years.
growth.source: Estimated from reed-stem Epidendrum culture and seed studies: orchidmall.com reed-stem Epidendrum notes (E. secundum canes 1-30 in, keikis on old spikes); symbiotic seed germination studies of Andean Epidendrum (e.g. E. geminiflorum, Ecuador).

epiphyte.name: Lowe's pitcher

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a tiny rosette of narrow leaves tipped with miniature pitchers. For years it stays a slow rosette making rounded, winged lower pitchers; then a stem up to 10 m climbs or hangs from mossy trees and makes the famous upper pitchers: hard, glossy, strongly waisted with a wide flared mouth and a lid bristling with white 'nectar' hairs under which tree shrews feed and leave droppings.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nepenthes lowii (1650-2600 m mossy forest, terrestrial or epiphytic; stem >10 m; gets 57-100% of leaf nitrogen from tree shrew droppings; raceme to 45 cm, capsules ~17 x 4 mm); growth and ages estimated from highland Nepenthes cultivation (very slow)

epiphyte.name: Vireya rhododendron

growth.juvenile_note: Vireya seeds carry a thread-like tail at each end and lodge in moss on branches or banks. The seedling is a tiny sprig of small, scaly, elliptic leaves; it grows in quick flushes, each ending in a whorl of glossy, leathery leaves, and becomes a loose, straggly, few-stemmed shrub perched on a mossy branch or rooted in the ground.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhododendron javanicum (evergreen shrub to 5 m, terrestrial or epiphytic; bright orange spring flowers; Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines); germination, growth and first flowering estimated from vireya growers' experience (seedlings flower in about 2-4 years)
